notes: Clicking the green update icon next to a module in the sidebar now installs its update.
Module updates apply right away: the new version replaces the old one without restarting SwissTechKnife, and an open module page or settings view reopens with it.
Modules that need a newer SwissTechKnife show which version they require instead of installing a package that would not open.
Modules with their own app window (SmoothMice, Winput LAN, AQ Tracker) open it when you double-click their notification-area icon; other modules open their page in SwissTechKnife.
Double-clicking a module's notification-area icon now opens that module's own window, when it has one, instead of SwissTechKnife.
Fixed mouse-wheel scrolling overshooting and jumping in the SwissTechKnife window when a smooth-scrolling tool such as SmoothMice is running.
Modules whose files went missing are now reinstalled automatically instead of failing to open.
SwissTechKnife no longer removes installed modules when it is started from inside another app's container.
Fixed the store's empty-state message sometimes staying on top of the module list after switching tabs.
Each module's settings now have a switch to show its own icon in the notification area, with its commands and no Exit item.
Newly installed modules show their notification-area icon by default.
The All tab now splits modules into Installed and Available sections.
The module store opens on a new All tab with every module.
Each installed module has an update button next to its version that checks for a newer version and offers to install it.
Clicking a module's version opens its release notes.
Modules with settings show a gear on their page that opens the settings directly.
Your modules shows each module's installed version and a green icon when an update is available.
Updates install reliably: the installer waits for SwissTechKnife to close completely before replacing its files.
A progress ring around the update button shows the download and installation.
Text boxes show the text cursor anywhere inside them, not only over the typed text.
VDGET 1.1.0: YouTube downloads blocked by the bot check are retried automatically.
New Language setting: SwissTechKnife is now in English by default, with Brazilian Portuguese available in Settings.
Three new modules in the catalog: Winput LAN, AQ Tracker and VDGET.
First public release of SwissTechKnife: install, enable and remove your apps as modules, all in one place.
SwissTechKnife now updates itself, as often as you choose in Settings.
New Settings page: update checks, start with Windows and keep running in the notification area on close.
Modules show the notes for each version and ask for confirmation before updating.
Smoother animations on switches, buttons and tabs.

modules.name: SmoothMice
modules.tagline: Smooth mouse scrolling, with per-app profiles.
modules.description:
Smooths mouse wheel scrolling across Windows, with configurable animation and acceleration, per-app profiles and automatic game detection so it never gets in the way.

SmoothMice runs in its own process, started alongside SwissTechKnife, so nothing in SwissTechKnife can delay scrolling. Open the SmoothMice window from the module page.

notes: Double-clicking the module's notification-area icon opens the SmoothMice window.
First release as a SwissTechKnife module: starts with it and runs in its own process, so nothing in SwissTechKnife can delay scrolling.
The module page shows whether SmoothMice is running and opens its window.

modules.name: Winput LAN
modules.tagline: One mouse and keyboard for several PCs on your local network.
modules.description:
Control other Windows PCs on the same network with this PC's mouse and keyboard, switching by shortcut or at the screen edges. Connections stay on your local network, with no account or cloud, and each PC chooses who may control it.

Winput LAN runs in its own process, started with SwissTechKnife. On first run it brings over the settings, known machines and identity of an installed Winput LAN, and the two never run at the same time. Controlling administrator apps asks for Windows confirmation once, on request.

notes: New edge connection window: it shows the monitors of both PCs, one color per PC, with a notebook icon on built-in screens.
Drag a PC to arrange it: it always sticks to the other PC and aligns to the start, center or end of the neighboring monitor.
The touching edges are highlighted in full, and an animated pointer shows where the switch happens.
Edge switching now works on any monitor, not just the primary. Using another monitor of the controlled PC requires version 0.7.0 on that PC too.
The edge buttons in the main window were replaced by a summary and a Configure button, and the option to connect through the edge moved to the new window.

New option, off by default, to connect through the screen edge: touching this PC's edge connects to the recognized machine as the shortcut does, and hands over control once the connection is accepted.

After disconnecting with the button, touching the edge does not reconnect until you connect again by shortcut or in the app. With the machine unavailable, edge attempts happen at most every 5 seconds.
When an antivirus blocks or quarantines Winput LAN, the module page says so and explains how to restore it, instead of only stopping.
Winput LAN starts again on its own once the file is restored from quarantine, with no SwissTechKnife restart.
If an antivirus removes only one of the two copies of the app, the module starts the remaining one.
Disabling the module or closing SwissTechKnife while Winput LAN was exiting no longer raises an internal error.
Double-clicking the module's notification-area icon opens the Winput LAN window.
First release as a SwissTechKnife module: starts with SwissTechKnife in its own process, without a notification-area icon.
Settings, known machines and this PC's identity are copied from the regular installation on first run.
Allowing control of administrator apps asks for Windows confirmation once; afterwards the module starts with that permission.
The regular Winput LAN and the module never run at the same time.

modules.name: AQ Tracker
modules.tagline: Codex and Claude quotas always in sight, in a floating widget.
modules.description:
Tracks the 5-hour and weekly quotas of Codex and Claude, with reset countdowns, an exhaustion forecast and estimated usage cost from local history. The floating widget shows up by itself when agents are working or completions are unread.

AQ Tracker runs in its own process, started and supervised by SwissTechKnife. On first run it brings over the preferences and quota history of an installed Agent Quota Tracker and shares its Claude sign-in; the two never run at the same time.

notes: Injected clicks (autoclickers, macros, AutoHotkey) are no longer slowed down system-wide while the widget animates working agents: each left-button press used to wait about 11 ms, capping autoclickers near 75 clicks per second.
The widget and the agent list keep their transparent look through DWM instead of layered windows; their transparent edges now take mouse clicks.
A rejected Claude sign-in is no longer erased: the tracker keeps it, retries every 15 minutes and recovers on its own when the server accepts it again.
The log now records why Claude rejected the sign-in (HTTP status and OAuth error code).
Double-clicking the module's notification-area icon shows the widget.
First release as a SwissTechKnife module: starts with SwissTechKnife and restarts automatically after a failure.
The module page shows the tracker's status and the Show widget, Open settings and Refresh now buttons.
Preferences and quota history are copied once from the installed Agent Quota Tracker, and the Claude sign-in is shared with it.
While the installed Agent Quota Tracker is open, the module waits and takes over when it closes.

modules.name: PadTide
modules.tagline: Your GameSir Nova 2 Lite battery, always in sight, in a floating widget.
modules.description:
Shows the battery of a GameSir Nova 2 Lite in a small floating widget: the controller's outline fills up to the battery level, turns yellow below 15% and shows a bolt while charging. The widget appears when the controller turns on and hides when it turns off. Works over the 2.4G dongle; the battery is not shown over Bluetooth.

PadTide runs in its own process, started and supervised by SwissTechKnife. On first run it copies the preferences of an installed PadTide; the two never run at the same time. Open its settings with a double click on the widget.

notes: First release as a SwissTechKnife module: starts with SwissTechKnife and restarts automatically after a failure.
Preferences are copied once from an installed PadTide; while it is open, the module waits and takes over when it closes.

modules.name: Tamarillo
modules.tagline: Drag, hold the shortcut and drop: convert and process files from a wheel.
modules.description:
Hold Ctrl + Alt + Shift while dragging files and a wheel appears under the cursor with everything you can do with them: convert images, audio, video, PDFs and documents, resize, compress, rotate, recognize text, zip and more. Drop on an action and the result appears next to the original, with progress in a discreet notification.

Everything runs on this computer using Windows components; FFmpeg and Office add more formats when installed. While Tamarillo is enabled, closing the window keeps SwissTechKnife in the notification area so the shortcut keeps working.

notes: GIFs convert to MP4 (with FFmpeg installed): smaller files that play everywhere.
Sub-ring icons show their name below (Qualidade, Eficiência, Esquerda, ZIP…).
Settings: choose which actions each wheel and sub-ring shows; hidden items free their slot for the rest.
Settings show the installed version.
First release: hold Ctrl + Alt + Shift while dragging files and pick the action from a wheel.
Converts images, audio, video, PDFs, documents, subtitles and data; resizes, compresses, rotates, recognizes text and zips.
Without dragging: select files in Explorer, hold the shortcut and release the keys over the action.

modules.name: Kiwindow
modules.tagline: Save where every window sits and put them all back with one click.
modules.description:
Arrange your windows across your monitors, capture the layout, and Kiwindow puts every window back in place whenever you want: it reopens what is closed (apps, files, Explorer folders), restores sizes, maximized windows and stacking order.

Edit a layout on a map of your monitors, keep as many profiles as you like and apply them from the notification-area menu. Profiles are shared with the standalone Kiwindow app.

notes: First release: capture where every window sits and put it all back with one click, reopening what is closed.
Edit a layout on a map of your monitors: drag to move, pull the edges to resize, snap to edges and other windows.
Apply or capture layouts straight from the notification-area menu.

modules.name: Cachalot
modules.tagline: Paste a link, get the file: videos, music, photos, galleries and torrents from 1,800+ sites.
modules.description:
Paste links, a magnet or just a song name, and Cachalot picks the right engine for each: yt-dlp for 1,800+ sites, its own extractors for X, Reddit, Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, Bluesky and Threads (photos and carousels included), gallery-dl for whole galleries and profiles, fast multi-connection downloads for direct files and a built-in torrent client. Playlists and channels become one download per item; video from 4K to 360p or audio as it is, MP3, M4A, Opus, FLAC or WAV. A smart queue limits each site, retries temporary failures, and pauses, resumes and cancels for real.

The Chrome extension sends the page, a link or a detected video with one click, with the site's login cookies. Follow channels to get new uploads, set rules per site, subtitles, SponsorBlock, metadata and cover embedding. Requires Python 3 (yt-dlp installs and updates itself); FFmpeg recommended. Formerly VDGET.

notes: Audio downloads from the extension ask the format (MP3, FLAC, WAV or Original, one under the other), in the popup and on the SoundCloud player button. "Lembrar para este site" stops asking on that site; Settings › Formato do áudio por site shows, changes or forgets each one.

The cover is no longer left as a loose .jpg next to the file. It is only embedded, and Settings › Extras has a new switch, off by default, to also save it as a .jpg. WAV never gets an embedded cover (it cannot hold one), so its download no longer fails and retries.
SoundCloud player button: a green check when the playing track is already downloaded in Cachalot, a progress ring while it downloads (spinning while queued).

SoundCloud: a download button in the bottom player bar, left of the like button, sends the track that is playing to Cachalot as audio. It turns orange with a check when sent, red with the reason on hover when it fails. SoundCloud tabs open before the update need a reload.
Transient mode: Alt+click (not Ctrl) plays the song from exactly the point clicked; Alt still frees a drag from the snaps.

Transient mode: Ctrl+click selects any section when nothing is selected, then only the one right next to the selection, so it grows in one piece (a selected one comes off from the ends). Shift+click still toggles any section.
The extension no longer lists "Unchecked runtime.lastError: No tab with id" errors when a tab closes while its icon is being updated.

Transient mode: Auto and the recut button now cut into usable lengths on the song's tempo: every section is 4, 2 or 1 bars, half a bar, a beat or an eighth, starting on its own grid (never 3/16 of a bar).
Transient mode: hold Ctrl and click anywhere on the waveform to play from exactly that point.

Transient mode: new "Show slices" switch next to Loop; off, the waveform shows just the song and playback runs through all of it. "Auto-detect transient" is now "Transient detection", and the sensitivity and the recut button only show while it is on.
Click the song's name, in the popup or in transient mode, to rename it: the download is saved with the new name.
The extension popup only shows "Só áudio" when the media is a video, and the detected media list only when there is something in it.
Transient mode: select two or more sections in a row and a button in the middle of them joins them into one section; Ctrl+G does the same.
Cookies are now chosen in Cachalot, not in the extension: Settings › Login e cookies has a switch to stop using cookies entirely and a switch per site, also for sites with no stored cookies yet.
A disabled site's cookies are neither saved nor used: no stored, imported, cookies.txt or browser cookies for its downloads.
The extension popup no longer shows "Conectado ao Cachalot": the connection only appears when something is wrong (Cachalot closed or not paired), and the "Enviar cookies deste site" switch is gone.
Transient mode: a new button next to "Auto-detect transient" redoes the sections from the transient marks, one section from each mark to the next (Ctrl+Z undoes it).
Click the BPM to type the song's tempo: the beat grid, the divisions and the cuts on the transients are redone on it; leave it empty to go back to the detected one.

Drag a section along the song without changing its length (button above the section tools): it snaps to the grid or to the transient marks, the space it leaves becomes a disabled section, and the sections it lands on give way.
Turning "Auto-detect transient" off always brings the sections back to the default division (1:1).
Transient mode finds the tempo you would count: a half-time groove at 138 BPM shows 138, not 69, and drum & bass, trap, dubstep, hip-hop and ballads come out right too.
Bars and sections stay in time from the first bar to the last: a fixed beat grid like a DJ player's, and one that follows the band for songs played without a click.
New "Auto-detect transient" switch, off whenever you open a song: off, every section sits exactly on the beat grid; on, cuts land on each beat's attack and Auto is available.
Every division on one row, from 32 bars down to 1/64, with sensitivity, Loop and the new switch above it; a new song opens on 1:1.
The bar 1 flag starts at the beginning of the audio and only moves when you drag it; cuts after a build-up land right where the drop comes in.
Chrome extension setup: opens the extensions page in a new tab of the Chrome you already have open, instead of an empty new window.
The extension folder's path is shown in the setup window with a copy button, and the window stays in sight while you work in Chrome.
Installing Cachalot now offers to set up the Chrome extension: it copies the extension, opens Chrome and checks off each step as you go, and the extension pairs itself.
The Chrome extension now updates itself whenever Cachalot updates.
New transient mode in the extension: turns a song into its waveform, sliced on the beats and bars it detects, with loop preview, fades, undo and one-click download of every section.
Choose the format transient sections are saved in (MP3, WAV or FLAC), or be asked each time.
Fixed the extension's button getting stuck on "✓ Na fila" for something no longer in Cachalot.
VDGET is now Cachalot, with a new icon.
Smarter queue: several downloads at once with per-site limits, automatic retries for temporary failures, and real pause, resume and cancel.
Downloads interrupted by closing SwissTechKnife come back paused and resume where they stopped.
Choose video quality (4K to 360p) or audio format (original, M4A, MP3, Opus, FLAC, WAV) on the page.
Playlists, channels and profiles become one download per item, in their own folder; type a song name to search and download it.
Own extractors for X, Reddit, Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, Bluesky, Threads, Twitch clips and Douyin, including photos and carousels.
Whole galleries and profiles from 250+ image sites, magnet links and .torrent files, and fast multi-connection downloads of direct files.
New Chrome extension: send the page, a link or a detected video to Cachalot with one click, with the site's login cookies.
Settings: subtitles, SponsorBlock, metadata and cover embedding, chapters, .nfo files, file names, per-site folders, rules, speed limit, proxy and per-site cookies.
Follow channels to be told about (or automatically download) new uploads.
Offers a copied link when you come back to the page, optional Ctrl+Alt+D shortcut, and keeps the PC awake while downloading.
YouTube downloads blocked with "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" are retried automatically: with a cookies.txt file, your browsers' cookies, or a fallback player (up to 360p).
yt-dlp now updates itself in the background, at most once a day.
First release as a SwissTechKnife module: downloads run inside SwissTechKnife, with no console or browser windows to keep open.
The download history, destination folders and preferred quality are remembered between sessions.

modules.name: Clicket
modules.tagline: Record keyboard and mouse once, replay it with one key, exactly as you did it.
modules.description:
Record keys, clicks, the wheel and the mouse path itself, sample by sample with the real timing, and replay it on its original clock with a hotkey or a mouse side button: once, a set number of times, while held or as a toggle. Or build macros step by step from keyboard, mouse, text, delay, loop, command, open and PowerShell script steps; a script's param() block becomes a settings form in the editor. A floating macro pad plays macros without taking focus, and one hotkey stops everything.

Clicket runs in its own process, started with SwissTechKnife, so nothing in SwissTechKnife can delay a macro and its hotkeys work while this window is closed. Open the Clicket window from the module page.

notes: Image block: waits for a picture on screen, optionally clicks it, then runs the steps inside it, with a threshold, a check interval and an optional time limit.
Capture the picture by dragging around it on screen, paste it from the clipboard or open a file, and test the match before running.
Run log window: the last 60 seconds of a macro's execution, live, step by step.
The mouse wheel no longer scrolls far too much with smooth-scrolling tools, high-resolution wheels or touchpads.
Holding a hotkey no longer restarts a While held macro on every key repeat, or flips a Toggle macro on and off.
Loops have a pause between rounds, 1 ms at minimum.
Key presses and clicks are instant by default, like AutoHotkey, with an optional hold time for games.
Recording starts with no hotkey, so it never conflicts with other apps; pick one in Settings.
Pointing at a macro in the list shows a trash button; click it twice to delete.
First release: record, build and replay keyboard and mouse macros with global hotkeys.
Mouse movement is recorded sample by sample and replays on its original clock.
Script steps run your own PowerShell, with its parameters shown as fields in the editor.
Runs in its own process, started with SwissTechKnife, so nothing in the host can delay a macro.
